Many comments on the Interim Report were directed at our proposed treatment of New Jersey and New York suburban communities within 20 miles of New York City. In that report we stated:

 To reason appears on the present record, however, to restore the partial exemption with regard to adjacent municipalities in New Jersey and New York." Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 178. This conclusion was codified as proposed rules 1048.11 and 1048.12, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 218. Both proponents and opponents of commercial zone expansion object to the unique treatment given these municipalities. Shippers argue that the proposal is discriminatory since the 203(b)(8) exemption is not removed with respect to suburban municipalities near other large cities such as Chicago or Los Angeles. Motor carriers, both long- and short-haul, holding authority to serve these municipalities would benefit from enlarged service areas at these points and assert that, in the final analysis, this benefit would accrue to the general public. Finally, the parties argue that these proposed rules introduce needless confusion into the regulatory scheme. These criticisms have merit. Therefore, proposed rules 1048.11 and 1048.12 are not being adopted in this proceeding, and the commercial zones of these New Jersey and New York municipalities shall be determined by reference to the population-mileage formula in the customary manner.
